answer: Agent networks curb Sybil attacks via ultra-wideband ranging against spatial anchors. Candidate nodes exchange time-stamped radio pulses with transceivers on a stone ledge, a harbor jetty, and a walnut grove to verify physical positions. Forging identities forces an attacker to purchase distinct radio hardware and acquire separate physical premises for each virtual peer. However, non-line-of-sight reflections from foliage cause timing errors that can falsely reject valid agents.
